nodes.description: Impaired SNARE-mediated fusion reduces activity-dependent neurotransmitter release, disturbing cortical synaptic transmission and activity-dependent brain development. This produces axial hypotonia from birth, intellectual disability, and autistic features with motor stereotypies; more severe C-terminal variants additionally cause central visual impairment, a hyperkinetic movement disorder, and epilepsy.

nodes.description: VAMP2 is one of the three core neuronal SNAREs whose zippering, triggered by the calcium sensor synaptotagmin-1, fuses the synaptic vesicle with the presynaptic membrane. Disease variants in the C-terminal SNARE motif impair vesicle fusion, as shown directly in a reconstituted lipid-mixing assay, reducing calcium-triggered neurotransmitter release. This is the module's key conformance target — the fusion-machinery arm.

nodes.description: De novo single-amino-acid deletions and non-synonymous variants affect conserved residues within the C-terminal VAMP2 SNARE motif — the region whose zippering with syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25 provides the energy for membrane fusion. VAMP2 is the vesicle-associated (v-)SNARE that is essential for vesicular exocytosis and activity-dependent neurotransmitter release, so these variants directly impair the fusion machinery.
